summary: Ran the full 18-case security regression suite against preview URL after the 2026-07 audit fixes. 17/18 pass. One CRITICAL PII leak still remains: /api/admin/analytics/student/{user_id} returns the raw user document (from admin.py line 964-972), which includes password_hash (bcrypt) and would also include admin_password/stripe_customer_id/push_token if set. Confirmed via live curl: leaked keys = ['password_hash']. All 11 pre-existing security_hardening tests still green (SEC-001 admin env-seeded login, SEC-002 discover/accepted/likes-received allowlist, SEC-003 bcrypt migration, SEC-004 ?token= rejection + CSV allowlist, SEC-005 chat plaintext filter, P3 headers + distance rounding + CORS regression guard). Added 7 new admin-side leak tests covering /admin/users, /admin/pending-verifications, /admin/university-admins, /admin/analytics/student/{id}, /admin/ai-risk-analysis/{id}, SEC-001 admin-login, and SEC-004 CSV token allowlist. Six pass; the analytics/student one fails and pinpoints the exact leak.

critical.issue: Returns raw user document in `student` field — leaks password_hash (bcrypt). Would also leak admin_password, stripe_customer_id, push_token if present on the doc. Regression: /api/admin/users was hardened with a projection at admin.py:109 but this sibling endpoint at admin.py:966 still does `db.users.find_one({...}, {"_id": 0})` and returns the whole thing. Fix: use the same _proj (password_hash, admin_password, stripe_customer_id, push_token = 0) as /admin/users.

minor.issue: Response includes `location` (GeoJSON {coordinates:[lng,lat]}) for each student. Uni admins are trusted, but precise coordinates are stalking-adjacent — consider stripping location or reducing to city label (same reasoning as SEC-002 P3-trilateration for peer discover).

action_items: PATCH /app/backend/routes/admin.py line ~966 in get_student_analytics: change `find_one({"user_id": user_id}, {"_id": 0})` to `find_one({"user_id": user_id}, {"_id": 0, "password_hash": 0, "admin_password": 0, "stripe_customer_id": 0, "push_token": 0})`. Same projection you already applied on /admin/users at line 109.

Optional: strip `location.coordinates` from /api/university-admin/students response (routes/university_admin.py line 133) — currently returns raw GPS to uni admin. Trust boundary is admin/uni-admin but P3 rationale (trilateration) still applies weakly.
critical_code_review_comments: Good: PUBLIC_PROFILE_FIELDS allowlist in matches.py is the correct pattern — projection-by-inclusion is far safer than projection-by-exclusion. Consider applying the same allowlist pattern to admin.py endpoints that return user docs.
Good: SEC-004 CSV allowlist verified — bogus ?token=deadbeef still 401s on /admin/export/students, real token 200s, and /admin/users?token= is correctly rejected 401.

Nit: /admin/pending-verifications includes password_hash in the query projection then converts to bool in Python (line 175-181). This is fine, but a single mistake (forgetting to pop it) would leak. Prefer `{'password_hash': {'$exists': True}}` projected via `$cond` in the query itself, or drop `password_hash` from the projection and use a second find with `{'password_hash': {'$exists': True}}`.

rca of the issue: SEC-002 fix (PUBLIC_PROFILE_FIELDS allowlist) was correctly applied to /matches/* peer-facing endpoints, and P3 hardening applied a deny-list projection to /admin/users. But sibling admin endpoints returning per-user documents (specifically /admin/analytics/student/{user_id} in admin.py line 964) were missed during the sweep — they still do `find_one({...}, {'_id': 0})` and return the raw doc into `{'student': student}`. Reproduction: 1) admin-login to get session_token, 2) GET /api/admin/users → grab any student user_id, 3) GET /api/admin/analytics/student/{that_id}, 4) response.student.password_hash is a bcrypt string. Mitigation: apply the same `_proj = {'_id': 0, 'password_hash': 0, 'admin_password': 0, 'stripe_customer_id': 0, 'push_token': 0}` used on /admin/users at line 109 to the find_one on line 966.
